rationale: Correct EdgeConneX's ownership and milestone history without creating duplicate platform records. Direct sources establish EQT Infrastructure as the continuing largest shareholder group, Sixth Street-managed funds as a current minority owner from 2024, Providence as the former seller group, and Liberty Global as a former minority holder that fully exited on June 29, 2026. CPP Investments funded EQT's broader AI infrastructure strategy but is not separately evidenced as a direct EdgeConneX shareholder, so it is not added. Sites, campuses, AdaniConneX and Chayora remain outside the canonical company boundary.

beforeImage.name: EdgeConneX
beforeImage.description: EdgeConneX develops and operates hyperlocal, hyperscale, and build-to-suit data center infrastructure globally. It serves hyperscalers, cloud providers, AI users, and enterprise customers requiring high-powered and purpose-built digital infrastructure. The business is asset-heavy and contracted because it develops and operates physical data center campuses under long-duration customer commitments. Company and EQT materials describe a global platform spanning more than 40 facilities in 33 markets across North America, Europe, and South America, with ongoing expansion into Asia and Europe. EQT Infrastructure announced the acquisition in 2020 and remains the owner through EQT infrastructure vehicles.

milestones.event: EdgeConneX expanded from an edge-focused footprint into a broader global hyperscale data center platform.
EdgeConneX announced completion of its acquisition by EQT Infrastructure.
EdgeConneX acquired Skellefteå Data Center Site from Lyten.
EQT introduced an AI infrastructure strategy with EdgeConneX as a core data center platform.

afterImage.name: EdgeConneX
afterImage.description: EdgeConneX is a global data-center developer and operator headquartered in Herndon, Virginia. Founded in 2009, it develops and operates edge, hyperscale, purpose-built and build-to-density facilities for hyperscale, cloud, enterprise, content, network, technology and AI customers. Public materials describe more than 80 operating or developing sites across over 60 markets in more than 20 countries, with over 10 GW of additional planned capacity. EQT Infrastructure IV completed the Providence-led acquisition on November 5, 2020; EQT Infrastructure V joined in 2021, Sixth Street-managed funds completed a minority investment in 2024, and EQT AI Infrastructure acquired a minority interest from EQT Infrastructure IV and V in 2026 while EQT remained the largest shareholder group. Liberty Global fully exited its former minority interest on June 29, 2026. CPP Investments' $1.75 billion commitment supports EQT's broader AI infrastructure strategy but is not disclosed as a separate direct EdgeConneX shareholding. Individual sites, campuses, subsidiaries, AdaniConneX and Chayora are outside this canonical company boundary. No later company sale, EQT exit, Sixth Street exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 29, 2026.
